notes:
- Extensions get a repository browser and real APK installs: A fifth tab browses Aniyomi, CloudStream, Sora and LNReader repositories, separates Anime, Manga and Novel entries, filters by ecosystem, language and NSFW, and installs an extension through Android's own package installer. It asks for the install permission when the phone has not granted it, offers the Settings ladder when a vendor build hides that screen, copies an APK from storage, and shows a restart banner so the install is registered on a fresh process. Two Aniyomi repositories are seeded, more can be added by URL or repository root, and the manager reports what is installed and what failed. This beta installs and records third-party APKs; executing their Aniyomi or CloudStream runtime is Phase 2 and the source sheet says so rather than showing a source that cannot play.
- A Watch flow for anime, with a source the app can actually play: The bottom of an anime's Info page now has a pinned Watch bar, and the Watch page that opens searches the selected source by the title's AniList name, draws the matched cover and title, and lists the episodes the source reports. Wrong Title? opens a real search against that source and remembers the result per title, so a bad match is one tap to correct. Episodes are grouped into All and 25-episode ranges, can be drawn as Minimal, Compact or Detailed cards, and carry their server count, duration and resume point. The beta's playable source is Internet Archive: it searches public-domain and Creative Commons animation and turns each file the item reports into a server. Aniyomi and CloudStream extensions installed from the Extensions tab are listed with their real install state and the Phase 2 note.
- A player with servers, next episode and a real resume point: Playback is Media3 ExoPlayer. The player lists every file the source offered as a server, remembers the chosen server per title, advances to the next episode when a file ends, and keeps the position in the title's Watch page as Continue Watching. The controls are the app's own - rewind and forward ten seconds, speed, fullscreen, next episode - and progress is written every five seconds and again when the player is closed, so a call or a crash does not lose the episode. The source and its file are named on screen; AniSequel hosts nothing.
- Player Settings draws the choices it can honour: Decoder, Video Renderer and Audio Engine are saved per device and shown on a Player Settings page reached from the Extension Manager and the player. The decoder choice filters Media3's codec selector, the renderer choice swaps a SurfaceView for a TextureView, and Anime 4K Enhancement applies the selected High-End or Mid-End colour grade through a real RenderEffect on the texture surface. That is a colour grade, not a spatial upscaler; the page's own note says so, and a true shader pipeline is Phase 3.
